candidate_bridge_statement: Every infinite compatible tail schedule over the LTE-closed graph must force either a high-valuation exit visible at some finite level or a Mersenne-style post-run descent event.
falsifiable_next_step: Search for compatible product paths whose finite prefixes avoid both high-valuation exits and the Mersenne post-run descent marker; any persistent family would refocus the obstruction.

observations.finite_signal: The largest saved LTE-closed tail graph has worst-case factor 1.2305030340113887 and lift-count typical factor 0.7516501240662575.
observations.missing_implication: A typical contraction does not exclude an individual compatible schedule that repeatedly selects high-growth edges.
observations.name: worst_typical_split
observations.next_test: Track whether high-growth product paths must eventually force a visible high-valuation exit in the tail coordinates.

observations.finite_signal: The constrained Karp product graph reports exact rational 3/4 at the largest saved product level, while the slope-constrained bounded scan has 1 survivor at its largest saved level.
observations.missing_implication: A period-capped balanced-word automaton does not cover every possible infinite compatible scheduler.
observations.name: compatible_product_graph
observations.next_test: Increase automaton period and slope precision together, and record whether non-elementary compatible cycles appear.

observations.finite_signal: The sampled Mersenne post-run table reaches descent below the start for R up to 90, with maximum measured post-run steps 155.
observations.missing_implication: Post-run descent rows do not contradict finite-depth all-one sieve survival, because they start measuring after the all-one branch has already been followed.
observations.name: mersenne_bypass_vs_post_run
observations.next_test: Attach each Mersenne post-run profile to the same compatibility coordinate used by the product graph, then check whether the forced post-run spike can be detected before descent.

thesis: The current diagnostics identify a single missing implication: finite or distributional contraction must be upgraded to exclusion of every individual infinite compatible schedule.
